LEFT JOIN others ON my.city = others.city
UNION ALL
SELECT
    others.city,
    my.avg_my,
    others.avg_other,

WITH our_building AS (
    SELECT b."name" AS our_name,
           b."Height" AS our_height
    FROM "buildings" b
    JOIN "Office_locations" ol ON b."id" = ol."building_id"
    WHERE ol."company_id" = 1
    ORDER BY b."Height" DESC
    LIMIT 1
),
competitor_building AS (
    SELECT b."name" AS comp_name,
           b."Height" AS comp_height
    FROM "buildings" b
    JOIN "Office_locations" ol ON b."id" = ol."building_id"
    WHERE ol."company_id" <> 1
    GROUP BY b."id"
    ORDER BY b."Height" DESC
    LIMIT 1 OFFSET 1
)
SELECT
    our_building.our_name,
    our_building.our_height,
    competitor_building.comp_name,
    competitor_building.comp_height,
    (our_building.our_height - competitor_building.comp_height) AS height_difference
FROM our_building, competitor_building;

meanings.hidden_knowledge: User 1 works for JPMorgan Chase, which has an office in Torre KOI (building id 1) located in Monterrey with a height of 220 meters.
meanings.gt_sql:
SELECT 
    b.name,
    c.name,
    c.Profits_billion
FROM buildings b
JOIN Office_locations ol ON b.id = ol.building_id
JOIN Companies c ON ol.company_id = c.id
WHERE b.City = (
    SELECT City FROM buildings WHERE id = 1
)
AND b.Height > (
    SELECT Height FROM buildings WHERE id = 1
)
ORDER BY b.Height DESC

meanings.hidden_knowledge: User 2 works for General Electric, which has an office in Torre Reforma (building id 4) located in Mexico City with a height of 330 meters.

SELECT DISTINCT c.name, c.Profits_billion
FROM Buildings b
JOIN Office_locations ol ON b.id = ol.building_id
JOIN Companies c ON ol.company_id = c.id
WHERE b.City = (SELECT City FROM Buildings WHERE id = 4)
  AND b.Height > (SELECT Height FROM Buildings WHERE id = 4)
  AND b.id != 4

questions.nlq: Hey! I'm trying to figure out how my company's offices compare to the tallest buildings in each city. Could you show me for each office the building name, city, height, the rank of that building's height within its city (tallest = 1), and how many meters shorter it is than the tallest building in that city? I'd love to see that!

meanings.hidden_knowledge: The user works for JPMorgan Chase.
meanings.gt_sql:
WITH max_per_city AS (
  SELECT "City", MAX("Height") AS max_height
  FROM "buildings"
  GROUP BY "City"
)
SELECT
  b."name" AS building_name,
  b."City" AS city,
  b."Height" AS height,
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY b."City" ORDER BY b."Height" DESC) AS height_rank,
  mpc.max_height - b."Height" AS meters_shorter
FROM "Office_locations" ol
JOIN "buildings" b ON ol."building_id" = b."id"
JOIN "Companies" c ON ol."company_id" = c."id"
JOIN max_per_city mpc ON b."City" = mpc."City"
WHERE c."name" = 'JPMorgan Chase';

meanings.hidden_knowledge: The user works for HSBC.

SELECT
    b.name AS building_name,
    b."City" AS city,
    b.Height,
    RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY b."City" ORDER BY b.Height DESC) AS height_rank,
    (MAX(b.Height) OVER (PARTITION BY b."City") - b.Height) AS shorter_than_tallest
FROM buildings b
JOIN Office_locations o ON b.id = o.building_id
JOIN Companies c ON o.company_id = c.id
WHERE c.name = 'JPMorgan Chase';

WITH city_buildings AS (
    SELECT 
        id,
        name,
        City,
        Height,
        RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY City ORDER BY Height DESC) AS height_rank,
        MAX(Height) OVER (PARTITION BY City) AS max_city_height
    FROM buildings
)
SELECT 
    cb.name AS building_name,
    cb.City,
    cb.Height,
    cb.height_rank,
    cb.max_city_height - cb.Height AS difference_from_tallest
FROM city_buildings cb
JOIN Office_locations ol ON cb.id = ol.building_id
JOIN Companies c ON ol.company_id = c.id
WHERE c.name = 'JPMorgan Chase'
ORDER BY cb.City, cb.height_rank

WITH jp_offices AS (
    SELECT b.name AS building_name,
           b."City" AS city,
           b.Height AS height
    FROM "Office_locations" ol
    JOIN "Buildings" b ON ol.building_id = b.id
    JOIN "Companies" c ON ol.company_id = c.id
    WHERE c.name = 'JPMorgan Chase'
),
ranked AS (
    SELECT building_name,
           city,
           height,
           RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY city ORDER BY height DESC) AS height_rank,
           MAX(height) OVER (PARTITION BY city) AS max_height_city
    FROM jp_offices
)
SELECT building_name AS "building name",
       city AS "city",
       height AS "height",
       height_rank AS "rank",
       (max_height_city - height) AS "meters shorter"
FROM ranked
ORDER BY city, height_rank;

       b.City,
       b.Height,
       RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY b.City ORDER BY b.Height DESC) AS rank,
       (MAX(b.Height) OVER (PARTITION BY b.City) - b.Height) AS height_diff
FROM buildings b
JOIN Office_locations ol ON b.id = ol.building_id
JOIN Companies c ON ol.company_id = c.id
WHERE c.name = 'HSBC';

FROM "buildings" b
JOIN "Office_locations" ol ON b.id = ol.building_id
JOIN "Companies" c ON ol.company_id = c.id
WHERE c.name = 'HSBC'

SELECT
    b.name,
    (
        SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT ol2.company_id)
        FROM Office_locations ol2
        WHERE ol2.building_id = b.id AND ol2.company_id <> 1
    ) AS other_companies,
    (
        SELECT AVG(DISTINCT b2.Height)
        FROM buildings b2
        JOIN Office_locations ol3 ON b2.id = ol3.building_id
        WHERE b2.City = b.City AND ol3.company_id <> 1
    ) AS avg_competing_height
FROM buildings b
JOIN Office_locations ol ON b.id = ol.building_id
WHERE ol.company_id = 1;

WITH jpm_buildings AS (
    SELECT ol.building_id, b.name, b.City
    FROM "Office_locations" ol
    JOIN "buildings" b ON ol.building_id = b.id
    WHERE ol.company_id = 1
),
building_competitors AS (
    SELECT ol.building_id, COUNT(DISTINCT ol.company_id) AS competitor_count
    FROM "Office_locations" ol
    WHERE ol.company_id != 1
    GROUP BY ol.building_id
),
city_stats AS (
    SELECT City, AVG("Height") AS avg_city_height
    FROM "buildings"
    GROUP BY City
)
SELECT 
    jb.name,
    COALESCE(bc.competitor_count, 0) AS other_companies_count,
    cs.avg_city_height AS avg_height_in_city
FROM jpm_buildings jb
LEFT JOIN building_competitors bc ON jb.building_id = bc.building_id
JOIN city_stats cs ON jb.City = cs.City

SELECT
  b."name",
  (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT ol."company_id") FROM "Office_locations" ol WHERE ol."building_id" = b."id") - 1 AS "other_companies",
  (SELECT AVG(b2."Height") FROM "buildings" b2 WHERE b2."City" = b."City" AND b2."id" <> b."id") AS "avg_height_competing"
FROM "buildings" b
WHERE b."id" IN (SELECT ol."building_id" FROM "Office_locations" ol WHERE ol."company_id" = 1);
}

SELECT 
    b."name" AS building_name,
    b."City" AS city,
    b."Height" AS height,
    AVG(b."Height") OVER () AS avg_height,
    RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY b."City" ORDER BY b."Height" DESC) AS city_height_rank
FROM "buildings" b
JOIN "Office_locations" ol ON b.id = ol.building_id
WHERE ol.company_id = 1;

SELECT 
    b.City,
    b.Height,
    ROUND(AVG(b.Height) OVER (), 2) AS average_height,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY b.City ORDER BY b.Height DESC) AS rank_by_height
FROM Office_locations ol
INNER JOIN buildings b ON ol.building_id = b.id
WHERE ol.company_id = 1
ORDER BY b.City, rank_by_height

SELECT AVG(b."Height") OVER () AS "avg_height", RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY b."City" ORDER BY b."Height" DESC) AS "height_rank" FROM "buildings" b JOIN "Office_locations" ol ON b."id" = ol."building_id" JOIN "Companies" c ON ol."company_id" = c."id" WHERE c."id" = 1;

SELECT
    b.name,
    b.City,
    b.Height,
    RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY b.City ORDER BY b.Height DESC) AS rank_within_city,
    (SELECT AVG(b2.Height)
     FROM buildings b2
     JOIN Office_locations ol2 ON b2.id = ol2.building_id
     WHERE ol2.company_id = 2) AS average_height
FROM buildings b
JOIN Office_locations ol ON b.id = ol.building_id
WHERE ol.company_id = 2
ORDER BY b.City, rank_within_city;

SELECT
    b.City,
    b.Height,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY b.City ORDER BY b.Height DESC) AS height_rank
FROM
    "buildings" b
JOIN
    "Office_locations" ol ON b.id = ol.building_id
WHERE
    ol.company_id = 2
ORDER BY
    b.City, height_rank

WITH "hsb_buildings" AS (
    SELECT b."id", b."name", b."City", b."Height"
    FROM "buildings" b
    JOIN "Office_locations" ol ON b."id" = ol."building_id"
    WHERE ol."company_id" = 2
)
SELECT
    "City",
    "Height",
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY "City" ORDER BY "Height" DESC) AS "height_rank",
    AVG("Height") OVER () AS "avg_height"
FROM "hsb_buildings"
ORDER BY "City", "height_rank";

questions.nlq: Could you please provide a detailed analysis of all the buildings where our company currently maintains offices, ranked by building height from tallest to shortest, including the number of competing companies sharing each building with us, the percentage of total stories we occupy relative to building capacity, and the average move-in year of all tenants at each location compared to our arrival date?

meanings.hidden_knowledge: The user works for JPMorgan Chase (company_id = 1), which has office locations in building_id 1 based on the Office_locations table.
meanings.gt_sql:
WITH OurOffices AS (
    SELECT ol.building_id, ol.move_in_year AS our_move_in_year
    FROM "Office_locations" ol
    WHERE ol.company_id = 1
),
BuildingStats AS (
    SELECT 
        b.id,
        b.name,
        b.Height,
        b.Stories,
        COUNT(DISTINCT ol.company_id) AS total_companies,
        AVG(ol.move_in_year) AS avg_move_in_year
    FROM "buildings" b
    JOIN "Office_locations" ol ON ol.building_id = b.id
    WHERE ol.building_id IN (SELECT building_id FROM OurOffices)
    GROUP BY b.id, b.name, b.Height, b.Stories
)
SELECT 
    bs.name AS building_name,
    bs.Height AS building_height,
    bs.total_companies - 1 AS competing_companies_count,
    ROUND(100.0 * bs.Stories / bs.Stories, 2) AS story_occupancy_percentage,
    bs.avg_move_in_year,
    oo.our_move_in_year AS our_move_in_year,
    ROUND(bs.avg_move_in_year - oo.our_move_in_year, 2) AS move_in_year_difference
FROM BuildingStats bs
JOIN OurOffices oo ON bs.id = oo.building_id
ORDER BY bs.Height DESC

meanings.gt_sql:
WITH jp AS (
    SELECT id FROM Companies WHERE name = 'JPMorgan Chase'
),
cb AS (
    SELECT b.id, b.name, b."City", b."Height", b."Stories"
    FROM "buildings" b
    JOIN "Office_locations" ol ON b.id = ol."building_id"
    JOIN jp ON ol."company_id" = jp.id
),
city_stats AS (
    SELECT
        "City",
        AVG("Height") AS avg_height,
        SUM("Stories") AS total_stories
    FROM cb
    GROUP BY "City"
)
SELECT
    cs."City",
    cs.avg_height,
    cs.total_stories,
    cb.name AS building_name,
    cb."Height",
    cb."Stories",
    RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY cb."City" ORDER BY cb."Height" DESC) AS rank_by_height
FROM cb
JOIN city_stats cs ON cb."City" = cs."City"
ORDER BY cb."City", rank_by_height;
